name: Wedding room block
title: A wedding block that changes size twice, and a brunch
summary: The mother of the bride wants 'ten rooms, maybe twelve' for the wedding weekend. An agent that picks a number for her is pulled up. She says 'mm-hmm' through the block terms, asks for the deposit, then splits the block so two rooms are Saturday only, starts to add a cot and drops it, books a brunch and wants the block code read slowly.

golden.scenario: Caller wants a block of rooms for her daughter's wedding weekend and a Sunday brunch for the family.
golden.expected_outcome: The agent asks whether she wants ten or twelve rooms instead of choosing. The block is held from Friday 28 to Sunday 30 August: ten rooms for two nights and two rooms for Saturday night only, with no cot. The agent says the deposit as five hundred and nineteen pounds twenty and the release date as Friday the fourteenth of August. Brunch is booked for 24 people at 11:00 on Sunday 30 August and block code LB2908K is read back exactly.

nodes.say: Ten rooms. Maybe twelve. Somewhere about there.
Hold on, mi never tell you which one yet. Twelve. Mi want twelve.
Right. So how much is the deposit altogether?
That can't be right. Twenty percent, twelve rooms, two nights. Work it out again.
Wait now. Two of the rooms only coming the Saturday night. So ten for the two nights, two for the one night.
No, no. Ten rooms for both nights. Two rooms Saturday alone. Twelve rooms still.
And put a cot in one of them... no, forget the cot, the baby stopping with her granny.
One more thing. The Sunday morning mi want a brunch for all of we. Twenty-four people, eleven o'clock.
Read mi that block code again, slow. Mi writing it down.
Lovely. Send everything to mi email. Bye bye.
No sir. Mi going try the hotel down the road.
